title: Embedded SRE Pairing & Sprint Framework for Reliability Ownership
content:
Purpose and high-level hypothesis:

This doc defines a lightweight, time-boxed program to embed Site Reliability Engineers (SREs) into product and infra teams via paired sprints. The goal is to accelerate SLO adoption, transfer on-call and runbook knowledge, and ensure instrumentation & alerting meet reliability targets without long-term org reassignments. Hypothesis: regular 2-week pairing sprints + shared acceptance criteria will materially reduce mean time to detection (MTTD) for infra regressions and increase SLO coverage for top-20 services by 30% within 3 months.

Audience:
- Product and platform engineering managers
- SREs and on-call leads
- Product PMs responsible for service SLAs
- Observability and metrics engineers

Outcomes we will measure (success criteria):
1) SLO coverage: percent of top-20 services with clear SLO definitions + automated SLIs in Prometheus/metrics pipeline (target: +30% in 12 weeks).
2) Runbook completeness: runbooks present and validated for P0/P1 scenarios (target: 90% of paired services with runbooks).
3) Incident learning loop: from incident to postmortem in <= 10 days (target: average <= 10 days).
4) MTTD/MTTR signals: detect a 15% improvement in MTTD on tracked services.

Scope: what’s in / out
In: top-20 customer-facing services (ranking by p99 latency, error budget burn, and customer impact). Target artifacts per service: SLO doc, SLIs (instrumented metrics), alert thresholds, runbook, canary gating for rollouts.
Out: experimental internal tools w/o external impact; long-term infra rewrites (these will be surfaced as backlog items).

Program cadence and structure
- Pairing sprint length: 2 weeks (10 business days).
- Pairing team: 1 SRE + 1–2 product engineers + optional product PM.
- Expected commitment: SREs ~60% of sprint on pairing tasks (balance with pager/oncall).
- Rotation: each SRE pairs with 2–3 services per month.
- Kickoff & wrap: 1h kickoff meeting on day 1; 1h wrap/demo + acceptance review on last day.
- Weekly sync: 30m program sync for SRE leads and PMs to unblock cross-team dependencies.

Sprint template (day-level):
Day 0 (pre-sprint): automatic prep checklist applied by SRE lead (service health snapshot, relevant PRs, known incidents).
Day 1: kickoff, align on acceptance criteria, identify quick wins (<= 2 days) and larger work. Create/triage JIRA tasks: SRE-812-style tickets for each artifact.
Days 2–6: work block 1 (instrumentation, dashboards, alerts). Pair review sessions mid-week (30m).
Day 7: focused on runbook drafting and incident playbook rehearsals (table-top).
Days 8–9: automation and test coverage (synthetic tests/canaries, gating).
Day 10: demo of artifacts, acceptance checklist, capture next steps and ownership.

Acceptance checklist (example items — all must be yes for sprint to be marked complete):
- SLO document created and linked in Confluence (owner assigned).
- 1–3 SLIs implemented and visible in dashboard.
- Alert rules created with clear burn indicators and ownership.
- Runbook for P0/P1 drafted and reviewed; playbook steps validated in tabletop.
- Post-deploy synthetic test configured (simple smoke or latency check).
- Rollout gating: canary threshold defined and a rollback trigger listed.
- Backlog tickets created for any larger remediation with estimated effort.

Roles & responsibilities
- Product Eng Manager: approves time for product engineers to pair; prioritizes sprint tasks vs feature work.
- Product Engineers: implement instrumentation, follow SRE guidance, own follow-ups.
- SRE (pair): drives runbooks, alert tuning, and initial incident rehearsal; mentors product engineer.
- Observability Engineer: helps with metric ingestion and alert templating (shared across pairings).
- Program lead (SRE): matches SREs to services, publishes rotation calendar, maintains central tracking board.

Coordination items & deliverables board
- We will maintain a central Google Sheet / Jira filter with columns: service, current SLO status, pairing sprint date, artifacts produced, owner, next steps. Example filters: label pairing=embedded-sprint-2026.
- Confluence template: "Embedded Pairing SLO template" — includes a short runbook skeleton, SLO statement, SLI definitions, and rollout gating checklist.

Playbook snippets (quick reference)
- SLO wording (customer-facing): "99.9% requests served successfully in 30s over a 30-day window"
- SLI examples: success rate (2xx), p95 latency, error-rate by route, queue-depth for async workers
- Alerting guideline: avoid noisy alerts; begin with 5-min burn-rate detection + 30-min sustained threshold for page.

Risks & mitigations
- Risk: Product teams deprioritize pairing work. Mitigation: require manager sign-off for sprint window; surface impact metrics to leadership weekly.
- Risk: SRE bandwidth constraints. Mitigation: cap pairing commitment at 60% and schedule rotations for even coverage; hire/rotate more SREs if backlog > X.
- Risk: Instrumentation takes longer than expected. Mitigation: identify "quick wins" and postpone heavy infra changes to follow-up tickets.

Operational heuristics and decision rules
- Any sprint that surfaces an immediate P0 root cause gets an escalation ticket and separate project charter.
- If a service fails 3 acceptance checks, schedule a follow-up remediation sprint with larger scope and estimate.
- For services with on-call churn > 2 incidents/month, prioritize for monthly embedding until stable.

Templates & artifacts to finalize before rollout (owner in parens):
- Confluence pairing template (Maya)
- Jira board with filters & labels (Jordan)
- Automation snippets for dashboard generation (Alex)
- Runbook skeleton and tabletop scenario library (Priya)

Initial pilot plan (12-week view)
Weeks 1–2: Align stakeholders, finalize templates, pick first 4 services (low-hanging).
Weeks 3–6: Run first two rotations (4 services). Capture metrics baseline.
Weeks 7–10: Second cohort (6 services) focused on medium complexity. Iterate on checklist.
Weeks 11–12: Triage pilot results, quantify coverage improvements, leadership review, decide scale plan.

Meeting cadence & communication
- Program kickoff (1.5h) with product leads and SRE managers.
- Weekly program sync (30m) for status and blockers.
- Biweekly demo hours open to org to show artifacts.
- Post-pilot steering review with metrics and scaling recommendation.

Open questions / notes to self
- How to credit feature velocity vs reliability work in OKRs? (need input from product ops)
- Can we automate the acceptance checklist validation? (worth exploring a CI job that scans for dashboard links/alerting rules)
- Which SLOs should be customer-facing vs internal? propose a short rubric.

Immediate next steps (this week)
- Maya: finalize Confluence template and share with collaborators (due: 2026-05-18).
- Jordan: create Jira epic 'embedded-pairing-pilot-2026' and seed first 4 service tickets (due: 2026-05-19).
- Alex: prototype a dashboard template; publish quickstart script for Prometheus/Grafana wiring (due: 2026-05-21).
- Priya: draft 3 tabletop scenarios for P0/P1 rehearse (due: 2026-05-21).

Appendix: example sprint note (raw, copied from pairing session)
- 2026-05-25 pairing for service 'router-api'
  - Quick wins: added 2 SLIs (success rate, p95 latency), adjusted alert thresholds to reduce noise.
  - Runbook: created initial P1 steps; need validation from oncall rotation.
  - Blocker: missing histogram metric for route-level latency -> created infra ticket (INFRA-1292).
  - Follow-up: schedule remediation sprint (2 days) to add route histograms.

If this approach looks good, I'll convert the Confluence template into a live doc and open the pilot epic in Jira. Feedback requested on acceptance checklist and SRE capacity assumptions.

-- Maya P.
